h2: Penetrant testing in Denver: dry-air dwell control, developer choice and aviation work
html:
Penetrant testing in Denver: dry-air dwell control, developer choice and aviation work

Penetrant testing around Denver finds surface-breaking cracks, porosity and laps on stainless and alloy welds, aluminum and other non-magnetic parts, and on any component where magnetic particle testing cannot be used. Atlantis sends PT technicians from Houston to Colorado sites, works to a procedure reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III, and trains technicians in the method for SNT-TC-1A certification.

Dwell control in dry, sunny air. Colorado's low humidity, altitude and strong sun make penetrant and solvent evaporate faster than they do on the Gulf Coast. A penetrant that dries on the surface during dwell will not draw back out of a fine crack, so a reliable outdoor procedure shades the area, limits the size of each section examined, and re-wets the surface if needed during dwell instead of letting it dry. Solvent cleaner should be applied to a cloth for excess removal, never sprayed straight onto the part, because flooding the surface washes penetrant out of shallow indications. These steps are written into the procedure and checked by the Level III, not left to the technician on the day.

Choosing the developer. The developer decides how well an indication is seen, and the choice depends on the job:

  • Nonaqueous (solvent-suspended) developer: the usual choice for field work with visible dye, applied as a thin, even spray coat.
  • Dry powder developer: used with fluorescent penetrant on production parts in a booth.
  • Water-soluble and water-suspendable developers: suited to penetrant lines where parts move through tanks after washing.

Ask a supplier which penetrant family, removal method and developer they propose, and why. A quote that says only "dye penetrant" leaves the sensitivity undefined.

Aviation in the Denver area. Southwest Airlines opened a Technical Operations hangar at Denver International Airport in March 2022 for scheduled overnight maintenance on its Boeing 737 fleet. Aviation PT follows the aircraft or engine manufacturer's NDT manual for the penetrant system, sensitivity level and acceptance limits, and aerospace production work requires NAS 410 personnel certification. Where an aerospace customer needs a NAS 410 Level 3, Atlantis arranges it through an associate.

Plant and boiler work. For boiler repairs, the state authority is the Colorado Department of Labor and Employment's Division of Oil and Public Safety, and workplace rules at Colorado plants are enforced by federal OSHA rather than a state plan. On stainless and nickel alloy piping, penetrant materials should be certified low in sulfur and halogens, as ASME Section V Article 6 requires for those alloys, and the batch certificates kept with the report.

The method and its limits are on the penetrant testing page, and site scopes are built from conventional NDT services. If your plant needs a PT procedure written for outdoor dwell control or a specific alloy, use NDT procedure development. To learn the method, use PT training and the Practical NDT penetrant simulator; enrollment for Colorado technicians is on the Denver NDT training page. Field PT bookings start with a list of components, alloys and target dates in the Denver PT request.
